user_clarification: The abandoned prepared-frame stale-data defect was on the CPU side.
mechanism: The viewer prepares an immutable CPU scene and matching input mapping for a future GPU submission. A failed preparation restores the last presented CPU mapping.
Before9b, scene deltas could already be consumed by the rejected preparation. Restoring the old CPU scene then applying only newer deltas could omit earlier changed records.
Display.take_changes_from(shown.seq) now checks the actual delta predecessor and forces complete source invalidation on mismatch. This recovers the lost CPU records.
GPU commands still used internally consistent submitted data. The defect could give those commands a stale CPU scene; it was not a partially updated GPU descriptor read.
gpu_control_contract: The three small camera/output uniform slots are immutable until their encoded commands are submitted. World and atlas are separate existing resources.
Queue writes after that submission are ordered after the earlier draws, so control storage can recycle without a GPU completion wait.

An atomic descriptor or pointer selects a resource/control version. It does not atomically publish all mutable world data or make updates immediately visible to every GPU operation. CPU publication, queue ordering and resource lifetime rules remain necessary.
scope: Clarification/source review only; no new code change or test execution.
